title: Tiny LSM Memtable Sizing
pattern: Setting memory flush buffers/memtables in LSM storage engines to excessively small sizes.
why_bad: Causes the engine to flush tiny, uncompressed files to mass storage continuously. This triggers severe disk write amplification, triggers constant background compactions, saturates disk bandwidth, and can exhaust system dentry/inode limits.
detection: LSM configuration parameters (`memtable_size_in_mb`) set to sub-megabyte or extremely small values relative to incoming write rates.
counterexample: Low-throughput embedded systems where disk I/O and RAM are strictly bound and writes are rare.
fix: Size memtables appropriately (typically 32MB to 128MB) to buffer a reasonable number of writes before flushing.
source: *Database Internals*, "LSM Trees," p. 132-135; *Building Secure and Reliable Systems*, p. 334.
